answer: Jury weight scales with independent path length, so an auditor six hops from the author counts for more than a neighbor one hop away, and a quorum must include subnetworks with no shared ancestry; because of that, a farm that fills one island of the graph cannot stack its own reviewers, and every verdict it wants has to be signed by a quill from a branch it does not own. The design still fails on a spiral-shaped graph where all long paths pass through one hub, so path length buys delay rather than immunity.
